## 2026-10-21 METR

发现 1 篇新文章:

**Review of the "Misalignment in high-stakes settings" section in Anthropic's Risk Report (August 2026)**
📅 Tue, 20 Oc
原文摘要：Scope and access: this review was written based solely on Anthropic’s internal Risk Report from August 2026 and is relatively lightweight. The authors of this review were engaged prior to the “ An update on independent evaluators ” announcement and did not have the level of access to information described in that post. We expect future engagements to be governed by different terms. Redaction summary statement: Anthropic had the right to veto publication of this review and to redact any part of it. No redactions were made to our review and we did not change any of our conclusions during the publication review process. METR made minor changes to our review in response to feedback from Anthropic, but these changes were limited to minor wording and clarification, as well as improving the methodology of an experiment we ran. Executive summary METR conducted an external review of the “Misalignment in high-stakes settings” section of Anthropic’s Risk Report: August 2026 . Anthropic’s report concludes that, as of July 15, 2026, “the risk of catastrophic harm caused by misalignment of [their] models is low.” Our best guess is that we agree with Anthropic that the risk of catastrophic harm from misalignment is low for the models covered in the report. However, this is primarily due to models’ limited capabilities, rather than safeguards and alignment training. We are not confident that, if risk were higher, the methodology in the report would reliably identify this. The report seems thoughtfully written and generally conveys uncertainty appropriately, but it is far from adequate for confidently ruling out misalignment. A strong argument would need much more extensive empirical work, and would require solving multiple open scientific problems. This is challenging given the pace of frontier development. The covert capabilities benchmarks in the report are a poor proxy for models’ ability to evade Anthropic’s internal usage monitoring system. They miss some ways models could eva
🔗 https://metr.org/blog/2026-10-20-misalignment-risk-report-august-2026-review/
